subject.title: /new and /reset should support @agent targeting in multi-agent channels

question: For destructive session commands in shared multi-agent channels, should OpenClaw require an explicit agent target, prompt for a target, or preserve route-derived defaults when `/new` or `/reset` has no target?
rationale: The remaining work changes command UX and the cross-agent session mutation boundary, so automation should not choose the permanent target syntax, ambiguity behavior, or authorization policy.

options.title: Require explicit target in ambiguous channels
options.body: Require `/new` and `/reset` to name a valid agent when multiple agents can receive the command, and fail closed or prompt when the target is ambiguous.

options.title: Prompt/select target on bare commands
options.body: Allow bare `/new` and `/reset` but show an in-product target chooser such as agent buttons plus an explicit all-agents option.

options.title: Keep route-derived default
options.body: Document current route-derived behavior and only add optional targeted syntax, accepting that bare commands can still affect the resolved route target.

recommendation.title: Require explicit target in ambiguous channels
recommendation.body: Require `/new` and `/reset` to name a valid agent when multiple agents can receive the command, and fail closed or prompt when the target is ambiguous.

likelyOwner.reason: The shared native-command session target resolver and recent shallow blame point to this owner path for a cross-channel command contract decision.
